articles.headline: ThorSport Racing Prepares Truck Series Promotion for Jake Bollman
articles.dek: The current ARCA Menards Series points leader is linked to the No. 98 seat for the 2028 campaign.
articles.body:
Garage whispers indicate that ThorSport Racing is positioning Jake Bollman for a full-time Craftsman Truck Series seat in 2028, with talks centering on the team's No. 98 entry.

Bollman has assembled a dominant campaign in the ARCA Menards Series, currently holding the championship lead with three wins and a 6.3 average finish. That performance has accelerated discussions between the driver and ThorSport management as the league reaches peak silly season ahead of the postseason cutoff.

While ThorSport has not scheduled a formal announcement, sources familiar with the discussions state that the framework of an agreement is taking shape. The move would secure Bollman's development path through the 2030 season, solidifying ThorSport's driver lineup across multiple years.

Bollman is also competing in the Craftsman Truck Series this season, sitting eighth in the championship standings with 417 points. His fourth-place run at Texas after starting 29th demonstrated his ability to manage traffic and race cleanly in truck competition.

ThorSport officials have declined to comment on future driver rosters. However, multiple paddock sources expect the agreement to progress from preliminary talks toward finalization before the regular season concludes.
articles.author: Cole Whitaker

byNumbers.label: ARCA Menards Series wins for Bollman

takeaways: Jake Bollman is in talks to take over the ThorSport Racing No. 98 truck full-time.
The potential deal is aimed at keeping Bollman under contract through 2030.
extras.whatsNext: Bollman will compete in the Black's Tire 250 at Richmond while silly season talks continue.

articles.headline: Chase Bubble Watch: Majeski Clings to Final Spot with Two Races Left
articles.dek: Stewart Friesen sits 18 points behind Ty Majeski as the series heads to Richmond for round 17.
articles.body:
Two races remain before the ten-driver Chase field is locked, and the cutline is razor thin. With Kaden Honeycutt scoring his second victory of the season at Daytona, nine of the available ten spots currently belong to race winners. That leaves a fierce points fight for the remaining territory as the series heads toward Richmond Raceway.

Ty Majeski currently holds the tenth and final transfer spot with 406 points, supported by one victory. Stewart Friesen sits directly below the cutoff in 11th with 388 points. Friesen failed to lead a lap at Daytona, finishing 13th, and now faces an 18-point deficit to Majeski with only Richmond and the regular-season finale remaining.

## The Winless Contenders

Jake Bollman occupies eighth in points with 417 tallies. Bollman remains the highest-ranked driver without a victory this season. His 29-point buffer over Friesen provides breathing room, but a new winner from below the cutline would instantly push Bollman into danger. Behind Bollman, Majeski's single win gives him an advantage on tiebreakers, but points accumulation remains critical.

Friesen's challenge is magnified by the drivers chasing him. Justin Haley holds 379 points, sitting nine back of Friesen and 27 behind Majeski. Corey LaJoie sits at 378 points after salvaging a tenth-place finish at Daytona. Parker Eatmon remains mathematically viable with 373 points, 33 back of the cutline.

## Short Track Outlook

Richmond Raceway changes the complexion of the bubble fight. The analytics model gives Ty Majeski a 9 percent chance to win at the three-quarter-mile track, third-highest among all entries. Friesen follows closely with a 7 percent win probability. If Friesen cannot secure a victory outright, outscoring Majeski by an average of nine points over each of the next two weeks is a tall order.

At the sharp end of the table, Chandler Smith leads the standings comfortably with 540 points and three victories. Grant Enfinger sits second with 469 points, followed by Ben Rhodes at 466 and Mini Tyrell at 458. For those frontrunners, the final two weeks of the regular season serve as preparation for the postseason grind. For Friesen, Haley, and LaJoie, Richmond is an absolute must-perform stop.
articles.author: Wes Ostrander

articles.headline: Kaden Honeycutt Outlasts Daytona Field in Marathon 250-Miler
articles.dek: Honeycutt led a race-high 73 laps and held off Christian Eckes by 0.629 seconds in a caution-heavy season opener.
articles.body:
Kaden Honeycutt kicked off the 2028 FedEx Freight Truck Series season with a dominant performance at Daytona International Speedway, taking the checkered flag in Friday's Fresh From Florida 250 by 0.629 seconds over Christian Eckes. Honeycutt started ninth in the No. 11 truck and paced the field for 73 of the 188 laps, controlling the late stages through heavy traffic and surviving repeated restarts.

The race became an endurance test characterized by attrition and pack racing, slowed by 12 caution flags across the 188-lap distance. Honeycutt showed the strongest package on the high banks, repeatedly cycling back to the front even as contenders reshuffled behind him. Eckes, who led 23 laps after rolling off fifth, mounted a late charge but could not find the push needed in the draft to displace the leader.

Behind the top two, Chandler Smith came from 20th on the grid to finish third, leading 18 laps during the afternoon. The drive of the day came from Mini Tyrell, who started dead last in the 37-truck field. Tyrell picked his way through multiple incidents, led 18 laps, and brought the No. 14 home in fourth position. Pole-sitter Ben Rhodes led 17 laps and crossed the stripe fifth, while Grant Enfinger, Cole Butcher, and part-timer Timmy Hill rounded out the group of drivers who spent double-digit laps out front.

The draft proved unforgiving for several entries who failed to see the finish. Mechanical failures sidelined Daniel Dominguez and Cleetus McFarland with transmission trouble, while suspension failures took out Andrés Pérez de Lara and Daniel Dye. Accidents eliminated Tyler Ankrum and Frankie Muniz.

With the victory, Honeycutt leaves Daytona leading the standings with 55 points, holding a 20-point advantage over Eckes (35) and Smith (34). Tyrell sits fourth with 33 points, followed closely by Rhodes with 32 points. Hill brought home an eighth-place finish, but as a part-time driver, he does not factor into the championship tally.

The Truck Series remains in Florida for the second stop of the 25-race calendar, shifting from the superspeedway high banks to the intermediate track layout at Atlanta.
articles.author: Jamie Kowalski

posts.text: Kaden Honeycutt takes the checkered flag at Daytona after leading 73 laps in a wild season opener. Christian Eckes finishes second, 0.629 seconds back.
KADENNNNN LETS GOOOO he actually did it 😭
Unreal. Another superspeedway race ruined by half a dozen cautions. At least the grill chicken turned out fine tonight.
Man, Honeycutt earned that one. Led the most laps and survived the chaos at the end.
survived is right, nobody could pass him on the outside anyway
He hit his marks every single restart though. Give credit where it's due.

posts.title: Daytona post-race thread: Fresh From Florida 250
posts.text: What an absolute marathon to start the year. Watched the whole thing with my boy and we were sweating bullets on those last three restarts. Honeycutt drove a masterclass out front.
masterclass? bro half the field crashed out or broke suspension
Staying out of the junk is part of superspeedway racing, you should know that by now. Friesen brought his truck home P13 and locked himself safely in the points bubble for now too.
Friesen only made it because Eatmon had a rough night. Let's not pretend it was a clean drive.
P13 is P13 on a plate track. I'll take it.
Mini Tyrell going from 37th to 4th is the drive of the night and you cannot convince me otherwise. Unbelievable charge through all that junk. Poll: who had a better race today?
People keep acting like Mini coming from the back is a shock when the 14 team has had race-winning speed all speedway season. It's all about fuel conservation early and tracking the middle lane.
sure grandma let's get you to bed. he missed three different wrecks by pure luck
Luck is when preparation meets opportunity. Check the lap averages before you talk.

posts.title: The 12-caution mess at Daytona
posts.text: my parlay was dead by lap 40 because of the perpetual yellow flags. 12 cautions is a joke man.
Bunch of kids driving over their heads as usual. Cole Butcher got screwed going a lap down because of that stackup in turn two. Started P8 and had nothing to show for it.
At least Butcher finished the race unlike Muniz and Ankrum. Could have been worse.
P19 is still trash for how fast the 13 was in practice.
Kaden Honeycutt is the first driver to win the Daytona season opener from a starting spot worse than 8th since 2021. Led 73 of 188 laps.
And yet people in the replies will still complain about the racing. Some of y'all just hate seeing anyone win.
Stat merchant posting numbers again. Give me some DFS value picks instead of historical trivia.
Fair enough, but Honeycutt was in my optimal lineup so I'm not complaining today lol

posts.title: Championship standings shape up after Daytona opener
posts.text: Chandler Smith sitting at the top of the points with 786 and four wins now. Man is putting together a proper season, playoffs or no playoffs. Back in my day we just crowned the guy with the most points at the end and went home.
yep playoff format ruins the whole deal. guys coasting all year until one race.
Chandler brought home P3 after starting 20th today. Solid day for the 38 team even if they missed out on the win.
starting 20th and finishing 3rd is decent fuel strategy I guess. still hate the format.
Hearing some early rumblings in the paddock about ThorSport looking closely at Jake Bollman for that 98 truck next year. Keep an eye on it.
Bollman was invisible all race today, what are we even talking about here. Give me some actual Silly Season news.
back in my day drivers had to win a race on merit before getting a top tier ride instead of just internet hype.
ok and? half the grid is pay drivers now anyway, let the kid cook if he has the backing.

interviews.quote: Starting 37th, you just hope to keep the nose clean, but the truck had huge speed once we got into the pack. Leading laps and bringing it home fourth is massive for our group.
The 11 was just too strong to crack on that final run. I thought we had the momentum on the outside, but nobody could get hooked up behind me.
We had the truck to beat all day and we knew it. With twelve cautions, you just have to execute every single restart and keep the lane covered. That is how you win at Daytona.

chase.headline: The Field Is Locked
chase.summary: The top 10 drivers locked in after race 18 with 2,500 simulated seasons confirming the cutoff. Chandler Smith leads the pack with 786 points and 100 percent odds, while Parker Eatmon sits just outside the cut in 11th with 600 points and zero percent odds.

notes.chandler smith: Chandler Smith holds the top spot with 786 points and a 100 percent chance to make the Chase.
notes.parker eatmon: Parker Eatmon is right on the bubble at 11th with 600 points and zero percent odds to advance.
notes.bryan dauzat: Bryan Dauzat sits 12th with 584 points and zero percent odds heading into the final stretch.

race.headline: Homestead Showdown Ready
race.summary: Grant Enfinger leads the win odds at 15 percent for the Craftsman 200 at Homestead-Miami Speedway. Meanwhile, Tyler Ankrum carries a heavy 68 percent wreck risk into the intermediate track finale.

notes.grant enfinger: Grant Enfinger tops the board with 15 percent win odds for the championship race.
notes.tyler ankrum: Tyler Ankrum brings the highest danger level of the field with a 68 percent wreck risk.
notes.andrés pérez de lara: Andrés Pérez de Lara trails close behind Ankrum with a 59 percent wreck risk.

season.headline: Smith Takes The Crown
season.summary: Chandler Smith is projected to take the title with 818 points and 100 percent title odds. Grant Enfinger rounds out the top two in the projections with 719 points.

notes.chandler smith: Chandler Smith cruises to P1 in the final projections with 818 points.
notes.grant enfinger: Grant Enfinger locks down P2 in the season projections with 719 points.
notes.stewart friesen: Stewart Friesen rounds out the top ten in the projections with 634 points.
